    Rule-Based Strategy Engine — Audit, Architecture and Implementation Plan

    Status: working design for the chosen build. It captures the current rule-based (non-trainable) engine, the target two-layer architecture, the impact analysis across every close path and every run mode (backtest, live sim, live real), the code-quality contract, and the per-method test plan. It is a standalone reference; it assumes no prior context.

    Related plans, audits, and current state (handoff)

    Entry point for the rule-based build line. Start here, then follow the links.

    Current state (2026-06-22)

    The Layer-1 regime/state + halving features are built and wired (the prerequisite flagged in §3.2):

    • MARKET_STATE (27 columns: continuous components, one-hot state flags, categorical codes, persistence / transition) and HALVING (8 columns) indicators exist across common / core / data-processing with green gates. MARKET_STATE consumes pre-computed ADX / EMA / ATR / Bollinger / close via eight single-column inputs (reusing cached parquets); HALVING is timestamp-only and symbol-agnostic.
    • The regime classification thresholds live once, in classify_regime_codes (modules/data-processing/src/rainbow/data_processing/indicator/market_state.py) — the single source of truth. scripts/analysis/regime/regime_detector_v2.py imports it (run alongside the original regime_detector.py; their labels agree).
    • The MEGA generator carries market_state / halving as catalog blocks disabled by default (every existing tier regenerates byte-identically) plus two new groups, full_single_tf_v2 / full_multi_tf_v2, that use them in place of the market_regime signals. A per-block columns list picks which columns become features (defaults: 10 for market_state, 3 for halving).

    Current implementation point (2026-06-27). Phase 1 (the shared predicate DSL) and Phase 2 (position-scoped CLOSE with RULE_EXIT and feature-context passing) are implemented, committed, and pass their gates; the torch batch evaluator lives in model-trainer and the action-rules config is optional. The full Phase-4 action set is implemented and gate-green: HOLD, FLAT_AT_TIME, book-aware ENTER_LONG / ENTER_SHORT, ADD, REDUCE, the protective updates (MOVE_STOP / MODIFY_TP / ENABLE_TRAIL / UPDATE_TRAIL), and REVERSE. The closing datetime / timezone consistency audit is verified. The Alembic migration for the protective and reverse schema is applied and verified — the trade_modifications table, trades.initial_take_profit, and the four action-counter columns on each session table now exist on the production database, added by a native ADD COLUMN (no table rebuild, no bloat), with every existing row left intact. The action engine is fully shipped, code and database.

    REDUCE is complete end-to-end: its config (reduce_size, a DSL formula in instrument units resolved against the rule context and bounded to the open interval (0, position size), and the shared rank_by / order / limit selector, plus the ENTER count), the trade split lineage (parent_trade_id / position_group_id / original_size columns with reduce_position and reduce_survivor), the bot-logic decision (the REDUCE order, the unified CLOSE / HOLD / REDUCE evaluator, the cross-position selector, and the book-state vocabulary in every rule context), and the order-layer execution split — a closed child slice plus a shrunk survivor — across backtest, live sim, and the live-real provider boundary (where a REDUCE is routed as a partial CLOSE). The invariants Σ size == original and Σ entry_commission == original hold, and the child's position-time-exposure interval is suppressed.

    An exhaustive unit and integral test campaign covers both layers: Layer 1 (rule_based contract, torch evaluator parity, the factory, parameter resolution), the DSL (operators, context edges, compiler safety, resolver), and Layer 2 (config validation, exit precedence, entries / ADD / selector, the REDUCE split in sim and real, and a per-action integral backtest → DB suite). All touched module gates pass.

    Three production defects were found and fixed during the campaign: the realized-PnL delta ignored REDUCE fills; the live-real provider request rejected the REDUCE action (routed as a partial CLOSE at the boundary); and position_bars_since_entry mixed a naive (DB-reloaded) opened_at with the timezone-aware tick clock — both sides are normalized through ensure_utc.

    The exit-reason distribution (ExitReasonStats / fetch_exit_reason_stats) now breaks out every shipped exit code into its own count (SIGNAL_FLIP, LOW_CONFIDENCE, RULE_EXIT, FLAT_AT_TIME, REDUCE, MANUAL), leaving other_count for unrecognized codes only; it needs no migration (recomputed from trades.exit_reason.code). The datetime / timezone consistency hardening is applied across the engine — the bot time scalars, the cooldown gate, and the exposure duration math all normalize through ensure_utc.

    The operational action counters reduce_action_count / add_action_count are wired end-to-end: the OperationalGateMetrics JSON sub-model, the runtime accumulator with pause / resume serialization, both engine loops, and the backtest_sessions / live_sessions flat columns — with no Trial.stage3_* mirror (an operational count is not a metric trials are ranked by), and the pre-existing stage3_risk_force_flat_count mirror is dropped. The Alembic revision for the lineage and counter columns is generated, reviewed, and applied: it adds parent_trade_id (self-FK) / position_group_id / original_size on trades, the two *_action_count columns on both session tables, and drops stage3_risk_force_flat_count from trials. The reconstructable counters are backfilled to their honest historical value (0 on every finalized session — these actions never ran before the engine existed; sessions left without a valid metrics payload stay NULL), writing both the metrics-JSON operational_gates block and the flat columns from the same validated object; trades.action_origin is normalized to its ENTRY default on historical rows.

    Protective-updates slice — complete, gate-green, and migrated. The four protective actions (MOVE_STOP / MODIFY_TP / ENABLE_TRAIL / UPDATE_TRAIL) and the automatic trailing stop are resolved on one protective channel, separate from the money-moving order channel, so a protective level change rides alongside the per-position money-moving action on the same tick and by construction touches no PnL / equity / metric. Built and passing every touched module gate:

    • The decision — BotLogic.generate_position_modifications folds the automatic trailing stop together with the rule protective actions into one PositionModificationPlan per position. Three independent protective axes resolve per tick: the stop takes the most-protective of the automatic trail and a rule MOVE_STOP (ties keep the trailing move, carrying its bookkeeping), the take-profit takes a rule MODIFY_TP, and the trailing configuration takes a rule ENABLE_TRAIL / UPDATE_TRAIL. Each value resolves through the §7.7 typed resolver (literal / formula / trailing_stop_config fallback, validated against its domain; a non-finite or out-of-domain result drops that axis with an audited rejection), and a move to the level already in place is a no-op — not applied, not audited.
    • The channel ordering — the protective decision runs in the loop's pre-exit slot (where the direct trailing write used to be), so a moved stop is consumed by the same tick's exit check exactly as before; the exit channel's arbiter.py::select_exit is unchanged (one money-moving close per position, strongest-first).
    • The execution in backtest and LIVE_SIM applies each plan to the in-memory position, persists the changed protective columns and the running extreme, writes one trade_modifications audit row per change, and increments the move_stop / modify_tp / trail operational counters (rule decisions only; the automatic trailing slide is audited with origin = TRAILING and never counted). In LIVE_REAL the running extreme (internal trailing state) is always persisted, but every venue-visible level change is routed through the provider (DataFetcher.submit_position_modification), which currently rejects it, so nothing is persisted and no audit row is written until the venue accepts — bringing the previously-direct live-real trailing write under the same gate.
    • The schema on disk — the trade_modifications audit table, trades.initial_take_profit, and the move_stop / modify_tp / trail action-counter columns on both session tables — plus the per-action, persistence, audit, and live-real-gate tests across common / database / core / bot-logic / backtesting-engine / live-trading-runner / data-fetcher.

    The old direct-trailing path (apply_trailing_stops, TrailingStopApplication, update_trailing_stop_state) is removed; the pure update_trailing_stop evaluator stays. REDUCE.size_pct is remediated to the §7.7 reduce_size formula end-to-end. The single Alembic migration for the protective and reverse schema (the trade_modifications table, trades.initial_take_profit, and the per-session action counters) is applied and verified on the production database via a native ADD COLUMN (no table rebuild, no bloat, rows intact).

    REVERSE — complete and gate-green. A REVERSE rule is position-scoped and always flips the position to the opposite side, so the side to open is derived rather than configured. The close leg closes the matched position with the REVERSE_CLOSE exit code, carrying the opposite side on Order.reverse_to_side, and the entry phase raises a risk-approved open leg on that side (REVERSE_OPEN lineage), sized off the post-close equity. The compound action is resume-atomic by construction: both legs queue with the same execute time and fill together on the next tick, so a pause never leaves a half-reverse. REVERSE_CLOSE is added to ExitCode and broken out in the exit-reason distribution; reverse_action_count is a session-metric column and runtime counter alongside the others; execution reuses the existing CLOSE and OPEN order paths across backtest, live sim, and the live-real provider boundary. Covered by per-action, config-validation, and a full-chain integral backtest test.

    The full Phase-4 action engine is implemented, gate-green, and migrated. Phase 3 (the optimization / run harness) is not built — only isolated foundations exist.

    Indicator catalog (2026-06-29) — complete: 34 indicators. Every classic indicator this plan called for now exists end-to-end (YAML defaults + IndicatorType + typed config + composed warm-up class + process_ / validate_ + dispatch + tests) across common / core / data-processing with green gates. The latest six were added on the same mold — Keltner Channel, SuperTrend, Ichimoku, Choppiness Index, Fractals, and Pivot Points — none of which TA-Lib provides, so each is computed with polars from primitives and each is lookahead-free (Ichimoku omits the forward-shifted cloud and the Chikou span, Fractals carry the centered-window confirmation delay, Pivots read the prior bar). IndicatorType lists 34.

    What remains is outside the core engine:

    • Open the rest of the catalog to raw rule features. The generator's rule_raw block currently exposes 14 indicators as raw (non-normalized) rule features — rsi, roc, ema, macd, adx, stochastic, willr, cci, mfi, ppo, trix, aroon, sar, linreg. The other indicators exist and run, but are not yet callable raw from a rule, so cci{-1} > 100 works while keltner_upper{-1} does not until added. Opening ATR / Bollinger / Keltner / SuperTrend / Ichimoku / Choppiness / Fractals / Pivots / VWAP / OBV / Volatility / Drawdown / Price-Oscillator (and the two-series Correlation / Ratio / Spread, which take a context symbol) to rule_raw is generator config, not engine work (§3.1).
    • Phase 3 (Optuna over rule parameters) is not built (the optimization / run harness above).
    • Running the vetted strategy battalion on folds is using the finished engine, not building it.

    Scope and priorities

    1. Core engine first. The deliverable that must be correct and complete is the two-layer engine — Layer 1 (rule_based on the shared DSL) and Layer 2 (the optional Bot Action Engine) — running in backtest and LIVE_SIM. These two modes are the bar and must be perfect: costs, slippage, exits, sizing, metrics, and the no-rules-equals-current-behavior guarantee.
    2. LIVE_REAL is out of scope to complete now. There is no exchange API / execution contract yet. The shared bot decision path already flows into the live-real adapter; wire up to that boundary but leave submit_order and the real-execution gaps not implemented — do not fake or force live-real. It is a separate, later prerequisite for going live (Section 8.2).
    3. Secondary, only after the core is solid: bot-override / strategy optimization (the bot-config optimizer and Optuna over bot action-rule parameters) and the MEGA-generator / feature-catalog wiring for rules (scripts). These improve strategies; they are not the core engine and must not be worked before the core is perfect.

    1. Purpose and Scope

    This is a research and build line, parallel to and separate from the thesis validation work (docs/plans/EXPERIMENT_PLAN_THESIS_VALIDATION.md) and the Script 2 ensemble work (docs/plans/SCRIPT2_CLOSURE_AND_NEW_ENSEMBLE_PLAN.md). Those lines test whether trainable models find signal. This line asks a different question with a different method:

    Can a catalog of deterministic, economically-motivated trading rules — optimized by Optuna and executed through the existing engine (costs, risk, metrics, walk-forward, traceability) — produce positive net edge, with no model training?

    The end goal is a vetted battalion of strategies that run first on folds and later on multi-year data. The catalog of which strategies to implement is a parallel research effort; this document builds the engine that can host the most complex strategies possible.

    2. How the Rule-Based Model Works (current state)

    2.1 Execution model and cost

    The rule_based model (modules/model-trainer/src/rainbow/model_trainer/models/rule_based.py) is declared non-trainable in the factory (is_trainable=False, has_pre_resolved=False). A run uses one trial, no epochs, no optimizer, no backward pass, and executes evaluation and backtest through the same infrastructure as the trainable models.

    Resource profile: no GPU; CPU/RAM/disk for feature computation, parquet IO, window building, and the per-tick backtest loop. The dominant cost for a large battalion is recomputing the same features many times; sharing feature packs across strategies on the same period and bounding parallel backtests keeps it tractable. Non-trainable does not mean zero cost, and it does not mean no overfitting (Section 6).

    2.2 Expression DSL

    Rules are expression strings parsed with Python ast in a restricted, safe mode. Function calls, subscripts, lambdas, and comprehensions are rejected. Supported elements:

    • Feature references with curly-brace timestep notation: feature_name{T} (for example rsi_14{-1} is the last tick in the window). Negative indices count from the window end and are validated against the sequence length.
    • Arithmetic operators + - * / **.
    • Comparison operators < <= > >= == !=, including chained comparisons such as 30 < rsi_14{-1} < 70.
    • Boolean composition with and / or and the bitwise & / | applied to boolean results.

    The current model configuration wraps each expression with a model payload: {expression, signal}. The expression itself is a predicate (true / false); the signal is not part of the DSL. In the rule_based model, predicates are evaluated in priority order, the first matching payload wins, and default_signal is emitted when no predicate matches (typically NONE). Evaluation is vectorized across the batch.

    2.3 Output contract and feature coupling

    The model emits the standard contract {logits, strength, quality} with three signal classes (NONE=0, LONG=1, SHORT=2). Because the contract matches the trainable models, the same scoring, bot logic, risk manager, backtest, and metrics apply unchanged. strength and quality are currently constant for the whole rule set.

    The model does not compute indicators. A rule referencing rsi_14 only works if a feature resolving to that name already exists in the experiment's feature window. Generator preflight compiles rule expressions through common.rules against the generated feature universe; missing or ambiguous features, invalid ranges, and unsupported syntax are rejected before a run starts. Rule-feature inputs must be raw (non-normalized) so thresholds such as > 70 remain semantically valid.

    Entry rules live in config/experiments/models/rule-based-model-hyperparameters.yaml (rule_based_model_hyperparameters.rules, a list of {expression, signal}), resolved into ResolvedRuleBasedModelHyperparameters (modules/model-trainer/.../types.py). This shape remains the Layer-1 rule contract: expression is evaluated by the shared predicate engine; signal is interpreted by the model layer.

    3. Feature Generation for Rules

    Feature blocks are built by the MEGA generator (scripts/experiments/generate/generate_mega_experiment.py). The Script 2 orchestrator delegates feature construction to MEGA via subprocess.

    3.1 The rule_raw block: palette and limits

    The _append_rule_raw_features function emits raw features named rule_raw_{symbol}_{timeframe}_{indicator} with an empty pipeline (no normalization), so classic thresholds (rsi_14{-1} > 70) stay semantically valid. It currently exposes 14 indicators toggled by include_* flags — RSI, ROC, EMA (fast/slow), MACD (line/signal), ADX (with plus_di / minus_di), Stochastic, Williams %R, CCI, MFI, PPO, TRIX, Aroon, Parabolic SAR, and LinReg — at one timeframe per experiment, per-symbol builder (BTC 5m shipped). Raw OHLCV is ensured as input but not exposed as a named rule feature. The remaining catalog indicators (§3.2) exist and run with green gates but are not yet in rule_raw, so they cannot be referenced raw from a rule until an include_<name> entry and its feature block are added here — generator config, not engine work.

    3.2 Full indicator catalog (34 indicators)

    The indicator library (modules/data-processing/src/rainbow/data_processing/indicator/) implements 34 indicators (every IndicatorType value). 14 are exposed raw to rules via rule_raw (§3.1); the rest run with green gates but still need a rule_raw entry to be callable raw from a rule. A sample of column sets and scaling (bounded ones take fixed thresholds directly; raw/price ones are used in comparisons):
